rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This continues 2:200’s division of pilgrims by their remembrance and supplication, adding hypocrites and sincere believers after the disbeliever and believer categories.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله تعالى : ( ومن الناس من يقول ) والجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿajjub literally involves perplexity from not knowing a cause; here it figuratively means that the eloquence and sweetness of his speech impress and magnify him, since its cause is known.
rows.anchor: وأصل التعجب حيرة تعرض للإنسان لجهله بسبب المتعجب منه وهو هنا مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean worldly affairs and means of livelihood, whether they benefit him or not; alternatively, al-dunyā is intended because his claim professes love and faith.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى ومنهم من يروقك ويعظم في نفسك ما يقوله : في الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the worldly-affairs reading, the phrase is a descriptive topic heading for his speech, with no ellipsis and an understood causal ظرف relation; it may instead modify يعجبك directly.
rows.anchor: وجوز تعلق المجرور بالفعل قبله أي يعجبك في الدنيا قوله لفصاحته

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq, who professed Islam to the Prophet, then burned Muslim crops and hamstrung their donkeys.
rows.anchor: والآية كما قال السدي : نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي حليف بن زهرة

words: ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes God as witness by claiming that God knows his heart agrees with his tongue; the clause coordinates with يعجبك.
rows.anchor: حيث يقول الله يعلم أن ما قلبي موافق لما في لساني وهو معطوف على ( يعجبك )

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy’s codex reads ويستشهد الله, presenting the man as calling God to witness.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي ويستشهد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with الله in the nominative makes God the witness and takes what is in the man’s heart as its true contents.
rows.anchor: وقريء ويشهد الله بالرفع فالمراد بما في قلبه ما فيه حقيقة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads والله يشهد على ما في قلبه; the clause is parenthetical, and على signals that the testimony harms the man.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما والله يشهد على ما في قلبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ألد الخصام as intensely contentious in falsehood.
rows.anchor: شديد المخاصمة في الباطل كما قال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: مهلهل
rows.claim: Alusi cites Mihlal’s verse, including خصيما, as poetic evidence in explaining the contentiousness expressed by ألد.
rows.anchor: وأستشهد عليه بقول مهلهل : إن تحت الحجار حزما وجورا وخصيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi takes ألد as an adjective like أحمر, not a comparative: it has plural لد and feminine لداء; its genitive construction links an adjective to its agent by figurative attribution.
rows.anchor: فألد صفة كأحمر بدليل جمعه على لد ومجيء مؤنثه لداء لا أفعل تفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the phrase mean intensely contentious in disputation, with a تقديرية ظرف relation.
rows.anchor: أي شديد في المخاصمة ونقل أبو حيان عن الخليل أن ألد

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān transmits al-Khalīl’s view that ألد is comparative, requiring an understood الخصام ألد or ألد ذوي الخصام; other proposed referents are strained, or خصام is a plural of خصم.
rows.anchor: ونقل أبو حيان عن الخليل أن ألد أفعل تفضيل فلا بد من تقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse signals that excessive quarrelsomeness is blameworthy and characteristic of hypocrites, who love worldly life and therefore dispute over it.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن شدة المخاصمة مذمومة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says, as narrated by ʿĀʾisha and recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim, that the most hateful men to God are the obstinately disputatious.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أبغض الرجال

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: A report from Abū al-Dardāʾ, recorded by Aḥmad, says persistent disputing makes one sinful and unjust, and persistent speaking makes one a liar, except speech concerning God.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد عن أبي الدرداء كفى بربك إثما أن لا تزال مماريا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets تولى as turning away and withdrawing.
rows.anchor: أي أدبر وأعرض قاله الحسن أو إذا غلب وصار واليا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets تولى as gaining power and becoming a governor.
rows.anchor: قاله الضحاك أن ( الحرث ) هنا النساء ( والنسل ) الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes الحرث as women and النسل as children.
rows.anchor: أن ( الحرث ) هنا النساء ( والنسل ) الأولاد

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq interprets الحرث as religion and النسل as people.
rows.anchor: وعن الصادق أن الحرث في هذا الموضع الدين والنسل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading makes the verb intransitive, with الحرث والنسل nominative and coordinated with سعى.
rows.anchor: على أن الفعل للحرث والنسل والرفع للعطف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan is reported to read the verb with fatḥa on lām, a dialectal form, and also with passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بفتح اللام وهي لغة أبى يأبى وروى عنه ويهلك على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not approve of corruption; the parenthetical statement warns of punishment, and mentioning فساد suffices because the general term includes the specific harms just described.
rows.anchor: لايرضى به فأحذروا غضبه عليه والجملة إعتراض للوعيد وأكتفى فيها على الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption is taking something from a praiseworthy state without a sound purpose, which is not found in God’s acts or commands; apparent corruption is relative to us, while all divine action is good.
rows.anchor: لأنه يقال : الإفسادكما قيل في الحقيقة إخراج الشيء عن حالة محمودة لا لغرض صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s destruction of animals for food serves humanity, the world’s central purpose; death also enables everlasting life and return to the original homeland.
rows.anchor: وأما أمره بإهلاك الحيوان مثلا لأكله فلإصلاح الإنسان الذي هو زبدة هذا العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When told to fear God in his conduct, the man is overtaken and surrounded by pride; العزة originally opposes humiliation and here figuratively denotes haughtiness and zeal.
rows.anchor: وإذا قيل له أتق الله في فعلك أخذته العزة أي أحتوت عليه وأحاطت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بالإثم can mean accompanied by sin or because of his prior sin.
rows.anchor: أي مصحوبا أو مصحوبة به أو بسبب إثمه السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further derivation takes أخذ as capture: pride and pre-Islamic zeal make him a captive shackled by sin.
rows.anchor: بمعنى السر ، ومنه الأخيذ للأسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary parsing makes جهنم the predicate and حسبه the subject, meaning Hell suffices him.
rows.anchor: جهنم ) مبتدأ وخبر أى كافيه ( جهنم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes جهنم the subject filling حسبه’s predicate position and treats حسب as an active participle; another takes حسب as a past particle meaning suffice, which Alusi questions.
rows.anchor: فاعل ل ( حسبه ) ساد مسد خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahannam is either the proper name of the punishment abode or of one of its levels, and is indeclinable because it is feminine proper name, on one analysis.
rows.anchor: علم لدار العقاب أو لطبقة من طبقاتها ممنوعة من الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr derives the name from a deep well, جهنام, and traces both to جهم, meaning aversion or harshness; Alusi rejects the proposed فعنلل pattern.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر إنها مشتقة من قولهم : ركية جهنام - إذا كانت بعيدة القعر وكلاهما من الجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view derives the word from Persian كهنام, Arabized by changing kāf to jīm and dropping alif; foreignness and proper naming then explain its indeclinability.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنها فارسى وأصلها كهنام فعربت - بإبدال الكاف جيما وإسقاط الألف -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase answers an implied oath; its omitted object of blame is obvious, and المهاد means bedding or what is prepared for the side, used mockingly.
rows.anchor: المخصوص بالذم محذوف لظهوره وتعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars distinguish a litigant’s rebuke to a judge: saying “be just” or similar may warrant discretionary punishment, but saying “fear God” does not.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال العلماء : إذا قال الخصم للقاضي : اعدل ونحوه له أن يعزره

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says one of the gravest sins is telling a brother to fear God and hearing him answer, “Mind yourself.”
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه ' إتن من أكبر الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended group is free divorced women who menstruate and whose marriages were consummated; unconsummated wives have no waiting period, nonmenstruating women wait by months, pregnant women until delivery, and enslaved women by two menstruations or two months.
rows.anchor: أي ذوات الأقراء من الحرائر المدخول بهن لما قد بين في الآيات والأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun is not universal, since the exceptions make universal application impossible; it denotes the relevant class, as in ordinary generic expressions.
rows.anchor: ههنا متعذر لما بين فتحمل على الجنس

rows.speaker: الحنفية
rows.claim: The Hanafis say the independent, unconnected statement abrogates the earlier general rule; abrogation requires that the earlier rule’s universal scope had first been established, which it was not.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب ساداتنا الحنفية لأن الكلام المستقل الغير الموصول عندهم ناسخ للعام

rows.speaker: الشافعية
rows.claim: The Shāfiʿīs treat المطلقات as general and say separately stated material specified some cases; al-Rāzī objects that specification is apt only when most cases remain, but Alusi rejects his unsupported criterion because general wording may be specified until a plural sense remains.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعية : إن ( المطلقات ) عام وقد خص البعض بكلام مستقل غير موصول وأعترضه الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتربصن means wait; the declarative predicate indirectly commands them, avoiding the need to reinterpret an imperative as a predicate. The alternative says the nominal sentence is declarative in form but imperative in meaning, which Alusi finds unnecessary.
rows.anchor: أي ينتظرن وهو خبر قصد منه الأمر على سبيل الكناية فلا يحتاج في وقوعه خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative form emphasizes certainty and urges prompt compliance; delaying the predicate after the subject adds emphasis, following a path discussed by ʿAbd al-Qāhir and al-Sakkākī.
rows.anchor: وتغيير العبارة للتأكيد بدلالته على التحقيق لأن الأصل في الخبر الصدق والكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ makes the women restrain themselves; the wording suggests their inclination toward men and their reluctance to wait, thereby exhorting them. The previous waiting command addresses husbands, for whom restraint is not shameful.
rows.anchor: النساء على التربصلأن الباءللتعدية فيكون المأمور به أن يقمعن أنفسهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثلاثة قروء is an accusative time expression; the transitive verb’s object is omitted, understood as marrying, or as the passage of the period.
rows.anchor: نصب على الظرف لكونه عبارة عن المدة والمفعول به محذوف لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object also suggests abstaining from marriage throughout the waiting period without even speaking of it.
rows.anchor: وفي حذفه إشعار بأنهن يتركن التزوج في هذه المدة بحيث لا يتلفظن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾ, plural qurūʾ, is more eloquently vocalized with fatḥa and ḍamma; it can mean menstruation or the purity between two menstrual periods.
rows.anchor: وهو يطلق للحيض لما أخرج النسائي وأبو داؤد والدار قطني

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubaysh, narrated from the Prophet by al-Nasāʾī, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Dāraquṭnī, uses qurūʾ for menstruation days when she should stop praying.
rows.anchor: لما أخرج النسائي وأبو داؤد والدار قطني أن فاطمة إبنة أبي حبيش قالت

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse uses qurūʾ for the women’s purity periods, since this is the time for intercourse, which is barred during menstruation even in pre-Islamic practice.
rows.anchor: كما في ظاهر قول الأعشى : أفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says the root indicates transition from purity to menstruation, which entails either state; a woman continuously pure or continuously bleeding is not called a possessor of qurūʾ.
rows.anchor: وأصله الإنتقال من الطهر إلى الحيض لإستلزامه كل واحد منهما والدليل على ذلك كما قال الراغب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says qurūʾ means the transition from purity into menstruation in one strong view, or the purity just left in his better-known view; it does not mean menstruation. He argues that menstrual onset signals the womb is clear, while purity onset may indicate conception.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقرء في الآية عند الشافعي الإنتقال من الطهر إلى الحيض في قول قوي له أو الطهر المنتقل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Shāfiʿī argument takes the lām in لعدتهن as temporal, making the waiting period the time for divorce and therefore disallowing divorce during menstruation.
rows.anchor: واللام للتأقيت والتخصيص بالوقت فيفيد أن مدخوله وقت لما قبله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that after he divorced his wife while she menstruated, the Prophet angrily ordered him to take her back, wait through another period and purity, then either keep her or divorce before intercourse; this is called the divinely prescribed divorce timing.
rows.anchor: إن إبن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما طلق زوجته وهي حائض فذكر عمر لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فتغيظ

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Shāfiʿīs also use the Ibn ʿUmar report to argue that the waiting period is counted by purity intervals.
rows.anchor: وهو أحد الأدلة أيضا على أن العدة بالإطهار

rows.speaker: الحنفية
rows.claim: The Hanafis understand qurūʾ as menstruations, following Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, and many others.
rows.anchor: وذهب ساداتنا الحنفية إلى أن المراد بالقرء الحيض وهو المروى عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi answers that, even if transition into menstruation identifies non-pregnancy, menstrual bleeding itself causes the desired clearing; the indicator is not preferable to the cause.
rows.anchor: بأن سيلان الدم هو السبب للبراءة المقصودة ولا نسلم أن اعتبار المعرف أولى من اعتبار السبب

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī says the lām marks association, which may mean an action occurs during, after, or before the reference time; the contextual cue here makes divorce occur before the waiting period.
rows.anchor: ففي الرضى إن اللام في نحو جئتك لغرة كذا هي المفيدة للإختصاص الذي هو أصلها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic reading, في قبل عدتهن, supports taking the divorce as preceding the waiting period; qabl means the front or what lies ahead.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم في قبل عدتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām need not mean that divorce coincides with the waiting period; the divorce occurs before it, as indicated by ordinary usage and the reading في قبل عدتهن.
rows.anchor: وفيما نحن فيه بقرينة تدل على كونه قبله لأن التطليق يكون قبل العدة لا مقارنا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the Ṣaḥīḥayn report does not prove that the waiting period is purity; that conclusion depends on identifying the demonstrative’s referent as purity, for which he finds no evidence.
rows.anchor: غير مسلم لأنه موقوف على جعل الإشارة للحالة التي هي الطهر ولا يقوم عليه دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative is feminine to agree with its predicate; when a pronoun lies between a masculine antecedent and feminine predicate, the majority prioritize agreement with the predicate because the past is fixed.
rows.anchor: وأنث أسم الإشارة مراعاة للخبر كالضمير إذا وقع بين مرجع مذكر وخبر مؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi allows the lām to mean either during or before, and reads the demonstrative as referring to menstruation: those are the periods before which women should be divorced, not while menstruating.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فتلك الحيض العدة التي أمر الله تعالى أن يطلق قبلها النساء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports a prophetic statement that an enslaved woman’s divorce is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstruations; Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, and al-Dāraquṭnī transmit it.
rows.anchor: وأما الإستدلال على أن ( القرء ) الحيض فهو ما أخرجه أبو داؤد والترمذي وإبن ماجه

rows.speaker: الحنفية
rows.claim: Hanafis infer that the free woman’s three qurūʾ are menstruations: free and enslaved women differ in waiting-period quantity, not kind, so the report clarifies the ambiguous term.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : طلاق الأمة تطليقتان وعدتها حيضتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi disputes dismissing the report as weak because its transmitter Maẓāhir was supposedly known for only one narration: Ibn ʿAdī records another and Ibn Ḥibbān authenticates him; al-Ḥākim reports no early criticism.
rows.anchor: لضعفه لأن فيه مظاهرا ولم يعرف له سواه لا يخلو عن بحث

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls the report gharīb but says scholars among the Companions and others acted on it; al-Dāraquṭnī reports Muslim practice, and Mālik says a report’s fame can replace its chain.
rows.anchor: قال الترمذي عقيب روايته : حديث غريب والعمل عليه عند أهل العلم

rows.speaker: الحنفية
rows.claim: Some Hanafis argue that if qurūʾ meant purity, the numeral three would be defeated because the common divorce period contains two full purities and part of a third.
rows.anchor: ومن أصحابنا من استدل بأنه لو كان المراد من القرء الطهر لزم إبطال موجب الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says this objection misstates al-Shāfiʿī, who counted transition into menstruation or the purity left behind, not the purity between bleeding episodes; entering the third can also count as three, as in calling a child three years old before completing the third.
rows.anchor: ناشيء من قلة التدبر فيما قاله الإمام الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه فلهذا اعترضوا به عليه

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī argues that qurūʾ means purity because the Prophet’s phrase “that is the waiting period” follows mention of a purity.
rows.anchor: الأقراء التي تعتد بها المطلقة الأطهار لأنه ذكر فتلك العدة بعد الطهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi replies that mentioning purity before the Prophet’s statement does not establish that purity is its referent; the menstruation bounded by purity may be intended.
rows.anchor: مجاب عنه بأن ذكره بعد الطهر لا يقتضي أن يكون مشارا إليه لجواز أن يكون ذكر الطهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the second purity is purposeful: if intercourse occurred during the first purity after reconciliation, a later purity permits a lawful divorce and shows reconciliation was not merely a device to divorce; time together may resolve the conflict.
rows.anchor: إذا راجعها في الطهر الأول بالجماع لم يكن طلاقها فيه للسنة فيحتاج للطهر الثاني

rows.speaker: الشافعية
rows.claim: Some Shāfiʿīs define qurʾ as menstruation bounded by two bleeding periods, extending it to some or all of the intervening purity just as water or honey names portions and wholes.
rows.anchor: قالوا : والإشتقاق مرشد إلى معنى الضم والإجتماع وهذا الطهر

rows.speaker: الشافعية
rows.claim: The Shāfiʿī derivation takes qurʾ to signify joining or gathering: blood gathers in the womb during purity, and all or part of that period equally indicates it.
rows.anchor: والإشتقاق مرشد إلى معنى الضم والإجتماع وهذا الطهر يحصل فيه إجتماع الدم

rows.speaker: الإمامية
rows.claim: The Imāmīs agree with this account and cite their own narrations from the Imams; reports attributed to ʿAlī on the question differ.
rows.anchor: والإمامية وافقوهم فيه وأستدلوا عليه برواياتهم عن الأئمة والرواية عن علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi judges the Shāfiʿī discussion strong after considering its full arguments and replies, though al-Kashshāf does not satisfy his inquiry; he offers this as a sufficient example.
rows.anchor: وبالجملة كلام الشافعية في هذا المقام قوي كما لا يخفى على من أحاط بأطراف كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the few plural aqraʾ might be expected, Arabic freely substitutes either plural pattern for the other. Qurūʾ suits all eligible free women collectively, whose three periods total many, and its plural marks that abundance.
rows.anchor: وكان القياس ذكر القرء بصيغة القلة التي هي الإقراء ولكنهم يتوسعون في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using أنفسهن instead of نفوسهن hints that divorce should be rare.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما أستعمل أنفسهن مكان نفوسهن للإشارة إلى أن الطلاق ينبغي أن يقع على القلة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar takes what God created in their wombs as pregnancy and menstruation: women must not hide pregnancy to avoid delaying divorce or stirring a husband’s compassion, nor hide menstruation to shorten the waiting period and defeat reconciliation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر : الحمل والحيض أي لا يحل لها إن كانت حاملا أن تكتم حملها

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: The interpretation including both pregnancy and menstruation is also reported from al-Ṣādiq, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and others.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو المروي عن الصادق والحسن ومجاهد وغيرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda restrict the phrase to pregnancy; Alusi answers that menstruation qualifies as created in the womb because it acquires its status there, even if the blood itself lies outside.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن ابن عباس وقتادة مدفوع بأن ذات الدم وإن كان غير مخلوق في الرحم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima argues that, since the passage addresses menstruating women, pregnancy cannot be intended and the phrase must mean menstruation; Alusi replies that externally limiting a general expression does not limit its referent here.
rows.anchor: وما قيل : إن الكلام في المطلقات ذوات الإقراء فلا يحتمل خلق الولد في أرحامهن

rows.speaker: ابن الفرس
rows.claim: Ibn al-Faras extends the verse to all matters concerning the private parts, including virginity, prior sexual experience, and defects, which women should be believed about; Alusi expresses reservation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الفرس : وعندي أن الآية عامة في جميع ما يتعلق بالفرج من بكارة وثيوبة وعيب

words: إن كن يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi marks the faith clause as a grammatical condition governing the following Quranic wording.
